-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in shallow water habitats.

## Natural history notes

A large wading bird characterized by its mostly white body, black flight feathers, bare dark head and neck, thick downcurved bill, and long legs. In Florida, it is found in freshwater and brackish wetlands, including marshes, cypress swamps, mangroves, wet prairies, ponds, impoundments, and shallow drying pools where prey becomes concentrated. It feeds mainly on fish, using tactile foraging by walking slowly through shallow water with its bill partly open and snapping it shut when prey touches it.
